stem:
Ammonium chloride, $\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}(\text{s})$, dissolves in water to form an acidic solution. This is due to the dissociation of the ammonium ions.

$$\text{NH}_4^+\text{(aq)} \rightleftharpoons \text{H}^+\text{(aq)} + \text{NH}_3\text{(aq)}$$

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.stem: The ammonium ion is a weak acid. The $\text{pH}$ of a $0.300\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ solution of ammonium chloride is 4.89 under standard conditions.
parts.text: Calculate the $[\text{H}^+]$ in a $0.300\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ solution of ammonium chloride.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the value of $pK_\text{a}$ of the ammonium ion.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem: A buffer solution can be made by mixing ammonium chloride with ammonia solution.
parts.text: Explain, with the aid of an equation, how this solution can behave as a buffer when a small amount of a strong acid is added.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Explain, with the aid of an equation, how this solution can behave as a buffer when a small amount of a strong base is added.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text:
Use the value of $K_\text{w}$ to calculate $[\text{H}^+]$ in pure water under standard conditions.

Show your working.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
The $\text{pH}$ of pure water at $50^\circ\text{C}$ is 6.64.

Calculate the numerical value of $K_\text{w}$ at $50^\circ\text{C}$.
